I know it’s not like me. But it feels like the role I spent my life building has been stripped away, and I don’t know how to behave anymore. It’s like I’m rebelling against my own life, and I don’t know how to stop.

I lost my job back in April, and after two months of sending out resumes and not getting responses—or getting ghosted after interviews—I just couldn’t handle living on my own anymore. I feel jittery, like I can’t sit still, and little things set me off—a phone call from an unknown number, even my mom checking in on me makes my chest tighten.

I keep thinking, “What if I never find work? What if I’m a burden?” It’s like everything is piling up, and I’m just not handling it well. I used to be confident, you know? I didn’t used to be this nervous, but lately, I’ve been anxious all the time, and it’s affecting my sleep, my focus—everything.     B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

It’s only been three weeks, but it’s like I don’t recognize myself. Losing my job didn’t just take my paycheck—it took my routine, my purpose. I’ve always been the guy who followed the rules, kept things under control. Now? I’m breaking them just to feel something.

D020_m047.question:
I’ve just been so overwhelmed since my son moved me out of my old home last month. I lived in that house for 47 years—every room held a memory, and now everything’s different. They put me in this assisted living place, all “for my safety,” but it feels like they took my freedom. I don’t need coddling—I raised three kids on my own after my husband passed.  

Lately, I’ve been sneaking out at night. I don’t see the point in asking permission—I’m not a child. I go to the diner down the street, have a cigarette, sometimes drive my car even though they said I shouldn’t. The staff act like I’m dangerous, but I’ve always been independent. I just… don’t feel like myself here.  

I’ve snapped at people—a couple times I threw a plate in the dining room when they tried to make me sit with the group. It’s not like me, I know, but I feel restless, angry. Like I’m not allowed to grieve or say no. This isn’t adjustment, it’s surrender. And I won’t give in without a fight.  

It’s only been a few weeks, but it feels like they’ve erased me. I want my life back.
D020_m047.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D020_m048.question:
I’ve been feeling off since I got back from my last rotation on the rig—about a month now. It started not long after we wrapped up a really rough stretch—a week of 16-hour shifts, constant storms, and one close call with a safety alarm that had everyone on edge. Since then, I just can’t seem to reset. I’m not sleeping well, even though I’m exhausted. My body feels tense all the time, like I’m still on high alert, but I’m not injured or sick—just… worn down.

I’ve been skipping out on hangouts with the crew after shifts. Usually, I’d grab a beer, blow off steam, but now I just want to be alone. I don’t have the energy to talk. My focus at work isn’t where it used to be—they even pulled me from a critical task last week because I was “too slow to respond.” That’s not like me. I’ve always prided myself on being reliable out there.

It’s not that anything catastrophic happened—just that the pressure built up, and now I can’t shake it. I thought it’d pass once I was back on land, but it’s only gotten worse. I’m worried it’s going to cost me my job if I can’t get back to normal.
D020_m048.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D020_m049.question:
I’ve been feeling really overwhelmed since my dad passed away a little over a month ago. I know everyone grieves differently, but it’s affecting everything—my work, my sleep, even little daily things feel impossible. I’ve been crying more than I ever have, and sometimes I can’t get out of bed until noon, which is not like me. I’ve always prided myself on being reliable—missing deadlines or calling in late, I just… never did that. But last week, I didn’t show up for a client review because I couldn’t bring myself to log in.  

I also feel this constant restlessness, like I can’t sit still. I’ve been snapping at coworkers—people I usually get along with—over small things. One minute I’m fine, the next I’m anxious, then numb. I’ve started drinking more than I should just to shut my brain off at night.  

Losing him was sudden, and since then, nothing feels stable. I can’t focus, I’m irritable, and I don’t enjoy anything—not my usual walks, not even the book club I helped start. I’m worried I’m falling apart at the worst time. My performance reviews are coming up, and I’ve never been this unreliable before.
D020_m049.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D020_m050.question:
I’ve been feeling really down and overwhelmed since I moved here about a month ago. My dad got transferred, so we had to leave my hometown, my friends, and the job I actually liked. Now I’m just working nights at this gas station, which wasn’t part of any plan. It’s not that I hate it—it’s just… I feel stuck. 

Lately, I’ve been sad for no reason. I cry sometimes when I’m alone, especially after a shift. I don’t know, it just hits me—like I’m never going to catch a break. I can’t sleep most nights, even when I’m exhausted. My appetite’s off, too. I used to enjoy playing video games or hanging out, but now I just go home and lie there. 

It’s hard to focus at work. I’ve messed up a couple times with the register, and my manager noticed. I feel like I’m failing at everything. I keep thinking this is never going to get better. I never felt like this before I moved—everything was fine. I just wish I could go back.
D020_m050.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
